mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.1% and 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5 for two consecutive months and 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase occur with 60-day forward returns negative in > 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer credit growth (RSAFS > 400) combined with expanding housing market (HOUST > 900) indicates robust consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high consumer credit and housing expansion
failure_condition: RSAFS > 400 and HOUST > 900 with 20-day forward returns negative in > 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO > 100) indicates expanding manufacturing output that correlates with stronger corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100 and 5-day forward returns negative in > 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0 for three consecutive months) signals overheating economy and impending central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0 for three consecutive months and 60-day forward returns positive in > 60% of cases over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5) defines a stable monetary environment that supports positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
regime_hint: low inflation and low rate regime
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5 with 60-day forward returns negative in > 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 6.5% for two consecutive months signals economic weakness that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 6.5 for two consecutive months and 5-day forward returns positive in > 60% of cases over any 5-year rolling window.
